'''Ōbashi no Mikoto''' (おおばせのみこと) was an influential figure of the [[Kofun period]] and an ancestor of the '''[[Nakatomi clan]]'''.

== Overview ==
Ōbashi no Mikoto is enshrined as a deity at {{ill|Ubuyu Inari Shrine|ja|産湯稲荷神社}} and {{ill|Himekoso Shrine|ja|比売許曽神社|qid=Q11547445}}. According to the Ubuyu Inari Shrine tradition, he was a 13th-generation descendant of [[Ame-no-Koyane]] and was born during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ar|الإمبراطور سيمو|arz|الامبراطور سيمو|azb|سیمو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Seimu|cs|Seimu|de|Seimu|es|Seimu Tennō|fa|امپراتور سیمو|fi|Seimu|fr|Seimu|hr|Seimu|hu|Szeimu japán császár|id|Kaisar Seimu|it|Seimu|ja|成務天皇|ka|სეიმუ|ko|세이무 천황|nl|Seimu|pl|Seimu|pt|Seimu|ru|Император Сэйму|sh|Car Seimu|simple|Emperor Seimu|sl|Cesar Sejmu|sv|Seimu|th|จักรพรรดิเซมุ|tl|Emperador Seimu|tr|Seimu (imparator)|uk|Імператор Сейму|uz|Imperator Seimu|vi|Thiên hoàng Seimu|yo|Emperor Seimu|zh|成務天皇|zh_min_nan|Seimu Thian-hông|zh_yue|成務天皇|qid=Q316672|lt=Emperor Seimu}} in the Ajihara district where the shrine is located. His father was {{ill|Ikadzuchi Ōmi no Mikoto|ja|中臣雷大臣}}, and his mother is identified as Kishi Kiyoo. He is said to have been the eldest of three brothers. Near Himekoso Shrine, there is a "Hōei Mound," where his placenta is said to have been buried.

== Genealogy ==
Ōbashi no Mikoto's father was {{ill|Ikadzuchi Ōmi no Mikoto|ja|中臣雷大臣}}, and his son was {{ill|Nakatomi no Amabisha-kyō|ja|中臣阿麻毘舎卿連|qid=DELETED_QID}}. His full brother was [[Maneko no Mikoto]], the ancestor of the {{ill|Iki no Sukune clan|ja|壱岐宿禰}}, and his half-brother was [[Nihon Ōmi no Mikoto]], the ancestor of the Nakatomi Kurihara clan<ref name="#1"/>.
